name: Lure cup
description: A hollowed case grown a fruiting body, turned over, and set down to wait — calling the whole time. The pod it replaces hid: its fuse was deliberately cold, on the reasoning that a magenta glow means something is calling the hive and you do not want your own trap advertising you. This is the opposite argument and the better one — a mine nothing walks near does nothing — so it wears the hive's colour and the scent goes out in rings. The scent used to be drawn here, as a soft bloom and two rings on the ground. It is not any more: from above, anything laid flat under the body reads as a cast shadow rather than as something leaving it, whatever colour it is — the same compositing problem that killed the rising plume before it. A pulse belongs in an `ss.fx.*` document that plays when the thing arms, not in the body's own parts, where it is on screen every frame doing the wrong job. It is the one thing in the arsenal allowed to be pink, because it is the one thing whose job is to be walked towards; it is bait in the player's hand rather than the player's voice, which is also why it is set down rather than carried. Upside down is what makes it a mine rather than scenery. A cap the right way up is a mushroom from any angle, and this game is played from above, where a dome is a dome. Turned over it is a cup: the gills face the sky, which is where the scent has to go anyway, and the stalk becomes a post standing out of the middle with the armed light on top of it. The inside is projected, not stylised. A gill is a straight radial line on a surface that rises as z = DEPTH*(r/R)^2 out to the rim; the camera foreshortens the ground by K and carries height up the screen, so each one lands as a parabola — the gills across the view bow hardest, the ones pointing at and away from it barely bend. The same projection puts the hub DEPTH below the centre of the rim ellipse rather than at it, and that offset is what sells the rest: the stalk climbs out of a low point you are looking down into. An earlier pass curved them by sweeping each seventeen degrees, which is a spiral — it says the gills turn, not that the surface falls away. The cap's outside hangs below the rim and ramps continuously from its bottom edge up to the shoulder. It is built as one dark base under fourteen thin layers of the same light at the same alpha, each stopping a little higher: a point near the rim lies inside every layer, a point at the bottom edge inside none, so the accumulation is the ramp and there is no step anywhere along it. Five opaque bands were the first attempt and each boundary read as an edge — the palette only holds five tones of pink, and a raw hex warns rather than resolving to a token. Gradients are the obvious tool and are the wrong one: the Phaser adapter has none, so a gradient fill flattens to its mid stop in the game while looking right in the gallery. Every band's top edge is solved to sit just under the rim's rather than being centred by eye. That is not tidiness: the outside of a cap is behind its own rim at this angle, and a band tall enough to rise above it lays its outline across the shoulder — which the first version did, in `$ink`, and the whole thing read as a sharp umbrella rather than as something swollen. The rim's own outline is a tone rather than ink for the same reason, and a lit sliver of shoulder shows under it where the surface rolls over. The white spots sit on that outside, each placed by solving the rim's lower edge and the cap's at its own x, so none can float off the body or hide behind the rim, and sized by how thick the band is there. Their sizes and heights are deliberately uneven: evenly spaced equal dots read as pearls set into the rim rather than as spots on a cap. The post is sampled off a half-width profile so it is a stalk and not a pin — narrow under the light, swollen through the middle, flared into the hub — and wears the stalk's own `$husk` rather than the grey it had, which belonged to trip-hairs and a machined band this no longer carries. Every pink surface sits one ramp step below where it started: the gill bed on `$pink.dark`, the rim band on `$pink.dark2`, and the belly's accumulation ramping toward `$pink` rather than `$pink.light`, so the shoulder stops about where it used to begin. The gills moved to `$ink@0.45` when the bed came down, because `$pink.dark2` against a `$pink.dark` bed is no longer two tones. What is deliberately not darkened is everything the body is there to carry — the scent rings, the bone stalk, the white spots and the armed light. A lure reads by contrast, not by being bright all over.
